library_preparation_preflight.summary: WebClient autoconfiguration itself needs nothing extra (JDK HttpClient connector is the automatic fallback, no reactor-netty required), but WebClientCodecCustomizer/WebClientAutoConfiguration$WebClientCodecsConfiguration reference org.springframework.boot.http.codec.CodecCustomizer, which spring-boot-webclient only declares as a runtime-scope dependency (not on the test-compile classpath) — the same situation spring-boot-restclient already solves by adding spring-boot-http-converter explicitly.

library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: No reactor-netty dependency is needed: ClientHttpConnectorBuilder.detect() falls back to JdkClientHttpConnectorBuilder (java.net.http.HttpClient) when no reactor-netty/Jetty/HttpComponents connector is on the classpath, so WebClientAutoConfiguration and ReactiveHttpClientAutoConfiguration activate fully from just spring-boot-webclient + its transitive spring-webflux/spring-boot-http-client. For coverage, exercise: WebClientAutoConfiguration (webClientBuilder bean, webClientHttpConnectorCustomizer via a bound ClientHttpConnector), WebClientObservationAutoConfiguration, AutoConfiguredWebClientSsl/WebClientSsl, ReactiveHttpServiceClientAutoConfiguration + PropertiesWebClientHttpServiceGroupConfigurer/WebClientCustomizerHttpServiceGroupConfigurer, and WebClientCodecCustomizer (needs the added dependency). Use a simple loopback com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer as the target, exactly like spring-boot-restclient's existing test, and remember WebClient calls are reactive — block() with a short timeout to get deterministic test results.
risks: 4.1.0-RC1 is a pre-GA release candidate; verify the dependency coordinate and package paths still match once 4.1.0 GA ships (other 4.1.0-RC1 Spring Boot modules, e.g. spring-boot-quartz, have already landed in this repo without issue on the same train).

Gradle's resolution of the published Gradle module metadata (not just the raw Maven POM scope) ultimately decides what lands on the test-compile classpath — confirm with an actual ./gradlew compileTestJava run that spring-boot-http-codec is indeed required and sufficient, rather than relying solely on POM scope inspection.
